First, we recall that SU(n) is the special unitary group, representing the symmetry group of an n-dimensional complex vector space. When n=5, SU(5) is the symmetry group of a 5-dimensional complex space. Spin(10), on the other hand, is the spin group in ten dimensions, fundamental in the context of ten-dimensional spacetime theories.

The formal proof references a Lie group homomorphism from SU(n) to Spin(2n) specifically for n=5. A homomorphism is a structure-preserving map between two groups, so in this case, it preserves the group operations while mapping SU(5) into Spin(10). 

This inclusion is non-trivial and comes from theoretical physics, particularly from the Georgi-Glashow model, which seeks to unify the strong, weak, and electromagnetic interactions. By embedding SU(5) into Spin(10), the model achieves a form of gauge symmetry unification, meaning that the forces described by SU(5) can be embedded within the broader framework of Spin(10) symmetries.

Thus, this result showcases the deep interconnections between group theory in mathematics and the foundational structures of the physical universe described by particle physics.

The special orthogonal group SO(10) has a spin group Representation, Spin(10), which is simply connected and double covers SO(10). Similarly, the special orthogonal groups SO(6) and SO(4) also have their corresponding spin groups, Spin(6) and Spin(4), respectively, which are simply connected.

This composition provides the explicit embedding needed to fit the Pati-Salam group within the Spin(10) framework.
